subject: Post-demo recap & probe runbook request — NovaScale latency/throughput
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Nguyen <caroline.nguyen@novascale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & probe runbook request — NovaScale latency/throughput

Hi Caroline — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed probe scope. Recording + assets attached (redwood-novascale-quick-comparison.pdf).

Recap (high level)
- Goal: validate production latency/throughput for NovaScale inference calls vs CloudTide across your representative prompt mix; confirm p95/p99 targets and cost/TP metrics.
- Evaluations discussed: 1) Redwood hosted inference (n1-standard variant we demoed), 2) CloudTide managed endpoint (Tim on cc), and 3) a reduced-precision quantized variant on NovaScale test infra.

Ask / proposed probe runbook (please confirm)
1) Dataset: 1k representative prompts (you said a 500–2k mix is realistic). We asked for sample file — you can drop it in the linked Drive.
2) Metrics: p50, p95, p99 latencies (server side), end-to-end wall time, tokens/sec (aggregate and per-request), success/error rates, cost per 1k tokens.
3) Test cases: a) single-request latency at low concurrency (1–4), b) sustained throughput (concurrency 16–128) for tokens/sec profiling, c) cold vs warm cache runs (KV cache disabled for a subset).
4) Variants: model v1 (baseline), v1-quant (8-bit), model small/large if you want to include in scope.
5) Duration: short smoke runs (1 hour) + 2 stress windows (2×30 minutes) per provider.
6) Reporting: CSV of raw samples + pre-computed p50/p95/p99 and histogram; short readout (30m) after runs.

Open questions for you:
- Finalized prompt set and any redacted-sensitive items (PII) we should remove before ingest.
- p95/p99 targets you consider acceptable vs must-have. You referenced p95 ~120ms in the call — want to confirm whether that was network-only or end-to-end.
- Procurement timeline: you mentioned a June PO target — can procurement@novascale.ai confirm expected decision date?

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Caroline: drop sample prompts and procurement timeline to the Drive by 5/24 EOD.
- Redwood (Marissa + Karthik): draft probe harness and parameter matrix by 5/25.
- Quick coordination call Wed 5/26 (15m) to lock final matrix and test windows.

Thanks — I can coordinate times and runbook docs.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

Vanessa / Caroline — following up with a concrete technical plan we can implement once we have the prompt set and sample sizes. I left a short checklist below for the probe harness.

Probe harness – minimal reproducible plan
- Driver: k6 + custom python client to call both Redwood and CloudTide endpoints (we’ll open-source the script snippets).
- Warmup: 200 requests across the prompt set to populate KV cache (where applicable).
- Run matrix:
  • Single-request latency: concurrency=1, run 1k requests across prompts -> collect per-request latencies (measure server-side and client E2E).
  • Burst throughput: concurrency levels 16, 32, 64 with run length 20 minutes each (record tokens/sec, error rates).
  • Sustained throughput: long run (60m) at estimated production concurrency for NovaScale (we should confirm, Caroline).
- Config: disable client-side retry throttles; set identical payloads across providers; for quantized variant ensure same model checkpoint ID where possible.
- Metrics to capture (minimum): p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, median tokens/sec, 95th tokens/sec, tail error codes, CPU/GPU util if we can get access to host metrics (ask Tim).
- Failure modes: network spikes, serialization errors, out-of-memory; capture stack traces where helpful.

Deliverables and timeline
- Redwood: probe harness + runbook (5/25) -> share as ZIP and Drive link.
- NovaScale: prompt set + procurement timeline (5/24).
- Run window: propose next week (5/31–6/2) for actual runs; we’ll schedule 2× 30m stress windows per provider.
- Quick readout (30m) on 6/3 with raw CSVs uploaded.

Questions for Caroline: can NovaScale provide (1) expected production concurrency per region and (2) whether we can request server-side GPU util for runs? Tim — are you ok to provide GPU util from CloudTide test endpoint?

Karthik
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
